messages.author: 833479854a80815e
messages.subject: rSPDE and bgev
parts:
Dear all, 

I am currently trying to use the rSPDE library according to the vignette: https://davidbolin.github.io/rSPDE//articles/rspde_inla.html

I want to check if my results obtained from library(INLA) get more informative related to the smoothness parameter when I set 

spde.nonstationary <- rspde.matern(mesh = mesh,
B.tau=cbind(0, 0, 0, 1, values_on_mesh),
 B.kappa=cbind(0, 1, values_on_mesh, 0, 0),
 theta.prior.mean=rep(0,4),
theta.prior.prec=rep(1,4),
rspde.order = 2, nu.upper.bound = 4 )

and then use the "bgev" distribution.
Unfortunately, I get the following error 
GitId: 8d82b7a3f8a7854799b4e1249e08cc8fd9e1350c  +0300
Error:12 Reason: The Newton-Raphson optimizer did not converge
Message: Condition `lambda < 1.0 / lambda_lim' is not TRUE
Line:1031 Function: GMRFLib_init_GMRF_approximation_store__intern

Segmentation fault
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

Do you know any workaround except for using a different EVD?

All the best, Corinna

P.S: it also did not work with the default values for rspde.matern

parts:
the bgev can be a little trick, as you might need to do this in two
steps, if you start far away from solution, or have a to flexible model

r = inla(..., control.inla=list(cmin=0))

r$.args$control.inla$cmin = -Inf

r = inla.rerun(r)
